1	"""Link-state neighbor discovery, LSA flooding and per-database SPF.
2	
3	This module models the link-state replay as deterministic synchronous rounds
4	over an explicit availability state (which nodes and links are up, supplied
5	by :mod:`packet_routing_sim.core.state`).  It performs no I/O of any kind and
6	depends on no dict insertion order: nodes and neighbors are always scanned in
7	sorted name order.
8	
9	An LSA is ``{"sequence": <int>, "neighbors": [<sorted names>]}`` and a link-
10	state database maps an originator name to the newest LSA held for it.  An
11	incoming LSA is accepted only when its sequence number is strictly greater
12	than the one already held for the same originator.  The link metric is the
13	single undirected topology metric, hence identical from both endpoints; a
14	link participates in SPF only while both endpoints' newest held LSAs still
15	declare each other.
16	
17	Round model
18	-----------
19	
20	* Round 0 is built explicitly.  At the fault-free start every online router
21	  discovers its available direct neighbors, originates a sequence-1 LSA with
22	  those neighbors sorted by name, and installs only its own LSA into its own
23	  database.  After an event the converged databases are inherited; online
24	  endpoints whose adjacency changed bump their local sequence (a recovered
25	  node continues from its own historical sequence) and install the new LSA,
26	  everyone else keeps the old view, and a recovered node otherwise starts
27	  with an empty database.  Down routers originate nothing and hold no
28	  database.
29	* Each later round every online router synchronously relays the newest LSAs
30	  it held at the start of the round over each currently available link; a
31	  receiver accepts only a strictly higher-sequence LSA from the same
32	  originator.  Rounds are recorded while any database changes, stopping at a
33	  fixed point.
34	
35	Every online router independently runs Dijkstra over its own current
36	database view, so a router that has not yet learned a newer LSA can briefly
37	keep an old route.  Equal-cost paths keep the smaller next-hop name.
38	"""
39	from .routing import forwarding_table
40	
41	
42	def make_lsa(sequence, neighbors):
43	    """Build one JSON-shaped local LSA with sorted neighbor names."""
44	    return {"sequence": sequence, "neighbors": sorted(neighbors)}
45	
46	
47	def copy_lsa(lsa):
48	    """Fresh copy of an LSA whose neighbor list shares nothing with the source."""
49	    return {"sequence": lsa["sequence"], "neighbors": list(lsa["neighbors"])}
50	
51	
52	def active_neighbor_sets(ordered_nodes, active_adjacency):
53	    """``{node: frozenset(its currently available neighbors)}``."""
54	    return {
55	        node: frozenset(active_adjacency[node]) for node in ordered_nodes
56	    }
57	
58	
59	def changed_endpoints(
60	    ordered_nodes, old_neighbors, new_neighbors, down_nodes, recovered=frozenset()
61	):
62	    """Online nodes whose discovered adjacency changed across an event.
63	
64	    This is every currently online node with a different available-neighbor
65	    set, plus every node that just recovered (even one with no live
66	    neighbors, so it still originates an LSA continuing its own historical
67	    sequence).  A node that went down is excluded: it originates nothing.
68	    """
69	    changed = {node for node in recovered if node not in down_nodes}
70	    for node in ordered_nodes:
71	        if node in down_nodes:
72	            continue
73	        if old_neighbors.get(node, frozenset()) != new_neighbors[node]:
74	            changed.add(node)
75	    return changed
76	
77	
78	def baseline_databases(ordered_nodes, new_neighbors):
79	    """Fault-free round zero and the initial per-node sequence history.
80	
81	    Every node originates a sequence-1 LSA and installs only its own LSA.
82	    """
83	    databases = {}
84	    sequences = {}
85	    for node in ordered_nodes:
86	        databases[node] = {node: make_lsa(1, new_neighbors[node])}
87	        sequences[node] = 1
88	    return databases, sequences
89	
90	
91	def event_databases(
92	    previous, ordered_nodes, new_neighbors, down_nodes, changed, sequences
93	):
94	    """Round-zero databases immediately after one failure/recovery event.
95	
96	    Online routers inherit the previous converged database (a recovered node
97	    starts with an empty one).  Each online endpoint whose adjacency changed
98	    originates its historical sequence plus one and installs that LSA as its
99	    own entry.  Returns the updated sequence history alongside; the history
100	    survives a node's downtime so a recovery continues the numbering.
101	    """
102	    databases = {}
103	    for node in ordered_nodes:
104	        if node in down_nodes:
105	            continue
106	        databases[node] = {
107	            originator: copy_lsa(lsa)
108	            for originator, lsa in previous.get(node, {}).items()
109	        }
110	
111	    next_sequences = dict(sequences)
112	    for node in sorted(changed):
113	        sequence = next_sequences.get(node, 0) + 1
114	        next_sequences[node] = sequence
115	        databases[node][node] = make_lsa(sequence, new_neighbors[node])
116	    return databases, next_sequences
117	
118	
119	def flood_round(previous, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, down_nodes):
120	    """One synchronous flooding exchange from the previous round's databases.
121	
122	    Each online router keeps its own previous database and accepts, from
123	    every currently available neighbor, strictly higher-sequence LSAs than
124	    the one it holds for that originator.  Every send reads only
125	    ``previous``, so no LSA travels more than one hop in a round.
126	    """
127	    current = {}
128	    for node in ordered_nodes:
129	        if node in down_nodes:
130	            continue
131	        current[node] = {
132	            originator: copy_lsa(lsa)
133	            for originator, lsa in previous[node].items()
134	        }
135	    for receiver in ordered_nodes:
136	        if receiver in down_nodes:
137	            continue
138	        held = current[receiver]
139	        for neighbor in sorted(active_adjacency[receiver]):
140	            for originator in sorted(previous[neighbor]):
141	                lsa = previous[neighbor][originator]
142	                known = held.get(originator)
143	                if known is None or lsa["sequence"] > known["sequence"]:
144	                    held[originator] = copy_lsa(lsa)
145	    return current
146	
147	
148	def _view_adjacency(database, topology):
149	    """Edges usable for SPF from one router's current database view.
150	
151	    A declared undirected link participates only while the newest held LSAs
152	    of both endpoints still name each other; the topology metric is the
153	    single shared metric the two declarations agree on.  A one-sided stale
154	    LSA therefore contributes no edge.
155	    """
156	    declared = {}
157	    for originator, lsa in database.items():
158	        declared[originator] = frozenset(lsa["neighbors"])
159	    adjacency = {node: {} for node in declared}
160	    for (source, target), metric in topology.links:
161	        if source not in declared or target not in declared:
162	            continue
163	        if target not in declared[source] or source not in declared[target]:
164	            continue
165	        adjacency[source][target] = metric
166	        adjacency[target][source] = metric
167	    return adjacency
168	
169	
170	def public_round(round_number, databases, ordered_nodes, topology):
171	    """Build one public round: ``round``, sorted ``databases``, ``routers``.
172	
173	    Every online router computes its forwarding table from its own database
174	    view alone; a down router has neither a database nor a forwarding row,
175	    both reported as ``null``.  All returned structures are fresh.
176	    """
177	    public_databases = {}
178	    routers = {}
179	    for node in ordered_nodes:
180	        if node not in databases:
181	            public_databases[node] = None
182	            routers[node] = None
183	            continue
184	        view = databases[node]
185	        public_databases[node] = {
186	            originator: copy_lsa(view[originator])
187	            for originator in sorted(view)
188	        }
189	        adjacency = _view_adjacency(view, topology)
190	        routers[node] = forwarding_table(node, ordered_nodes, adjacency)
191	    return {"round": round_number, "databases": public_databases, "routers": routers}
192	
193	
194	def link_state_convergence(round_zero, ordered_nodes, topology, active_adjacency, down_nodes):
195	    """Record round 0 and every later round in which a database changes.
196	
197	    Returns ``(rounds, final_databases)`` so a replay can inherit the fixed
198	    point as the next event's round-zero basis.  Flooding only ever raises a
199	    held sequence toward a finite ceiling (one bounded counter per
200	    originator, exchanged inside finite components), so the scan always
201	    reaches a fixed point.
202	    """
203	    rounds = [public_round(0, round_zero, ordered_nodes, topology)]
204	    databases = round_zero
205	    while True:
206	        updated = flood_round(
207	            databases, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, down_nodes
208	        )
209	        if updated == databases:
210	            break
211	        databases = updated
212	        rounds.append(
213	            public_round(len(rounds), databases, ordered_nodes, topology)
214	        )
215	    return rounds, databases

1	"""Routing computations over an explicit topology/availability state.
2	
3	Two protocols live here:
4	
5	* link-state shortest-path forwarding tables (Dijkstra) used by ``compute``
6	  and every replay snapshot;
7	* synchronous distance-vector rounds used by ``converge``.
8	
9	Both are pure functions of the supplied adjacency map and ordered node
10	tuple.  Neighbors are always iterated in sorted name order and equal-metric
11	choices use a strict comparison, so ties deterministically select the
12	smaller next-hop name regardless of dict insertion order or hash seed.
13	"""
14	import heapq
15	
16	
17	def forwarding_table(source, ordered_nodes, adjacency):
18	    """Dijkstra from ``source``; ties on total metric pick the smaller hop."""
19	    distances = {source: 0}
20	    next_hops = {}
21	    # Label is (total metric, first hop name); "" is a sentinel for the source
22	    # and sorts before any real (necessarily non-empty) node name.
23	    heap = [(0, "", source)]
24	    settled = set()
25	    while heap:
26	        distance, first_hop, node = heapq.heappop(heap)
27	        if node in settled:
28	            continue
29	        settled.add(node)
30	        distances[node] = distance
31	        next_hops[node] = first_hop
32	        for neighbor in sorted(adjacency[node]):
33	            if neighbor in settled:
34	                continue
35	            metric = adjacency[node][neighbor]
36	            candidate = distance + metric
37	            candidate_hop = neighbor if node == source else first_hop
38	            heapq.heappush(heap, (candidate, candidate_hop, neighbor))
39	
40	    table = {}
41	    for destination in ordered_nodes:
42	        if destination == source:
43	            table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0}
44	        elif destination in distances:
45	            table[destination] = {
46	                "nextHop": next_hops[destination],
47	                "metric": distances[destination],
48	            }
49	        else:
50	            table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
51	    return table
52	
53	
54	def link_state_snapshot(ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, down_nodes):
55	    """Forwarding tables for every node from an availability state.
56	
57	    Up routers are computed against the subgraph of usable links; a down
58	    router's whole row is ``null``/``null``.  Destinations that are down or
59	    unreachable likewise come out ``null``/``null`` from Dijkstra.
60	    """
61	    routers = {}
62	    for source in ordered_nodes:
63	        if source in down_nodes:
64	            routers[source] = {
65	                destination: {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
66	                for destination in ordered_nodes
67	            }
68	        else:
69	            routers[source] = forwarding_table(
70	                source, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency
71	            )
72	    return routers
73	
74	
75	def initial_distance_vectors(ordered_nodes, adjacency):
76	    """Round 0: each router knows only itself and its directly connected links."""
77	    vectors = {}
78	    for router in ordered_nodes:
79	        table = {}
80	        for destination in ordered_nodes:
81	            if destination == router:
82	                table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0}
83	            elif destination in adjacency[router]:
84	                table[destination] = {
85	                    "nextHop": destination,
86	                    "metric": adjacency[router][destination],
87	                }
88	            else:
89	                table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
90	        vectors[router] = table
91	    return vectors

95	    """Synchronously update every router from the previous round's ads."""
96	    current = {}
97	    for router in ordered_nodes:
98	        table = {}
99	        for destination in ordered_nodes:
100	            if destination == router:
101	                table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0}
102	                continue
103	            best_metric = None
104	            best_hop = None
105	            for neighbor in sorted(adjacency[router]):
106	                advertised = previous[neighbor][destination]
107	                if advertised["metric"] is None:

109	                candidate = adjacency[router][neighbor] + advertised["metric"]
110	                # Neighbors are iterated in name order, so the first best
111	                # candidate keeps the smaller next-hop name on ties.
112	                if best_metric is None or candidate < best_metric:
113	                    best_metric = candidate
114	                    best_hop = neighbor
115	            if best_metric is None:
116	                table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
117	            else:
118	                table[destination] = {"nextHop": best_hop, "metric": best_metric}
119	        current[router] = table
120	    return current
121	
122	
123	def distance_vector_convergence(ordered_nodes, adjacency):
124	    """Return every changed synchronous round from round 0 to a fixed point."""
125	    vectors = initial_distance_vectors(ordered_nodes, adjacency)
126	    rounds = [{"round": 0, "routers": vectors}]
127	    while True:
128	        updated = distance_vector_round(vectors, ordered_nodes, adjacency)
129	        if updated == vectors:
130	            break
131	        vectors = updated
132	        rounds.append({"round": len(rounds), "routers": vectors})
133	    return rounds
134	
135	
136	def _unreachable_row(ordered_nodes):
137	    """A fresh row advertising every destination (including self) as down."""
138	    return {
139	        destination: {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
140	        for destination in ordered_nodes
141	    }

144	def distance_vector_failure_round_zero(
145	    previous, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, down_nodes
146	):
147	    """Round 0 immediately after a failure/recovery event.
148	
149	    Every online router keeps the routes it advertised in the previous
150	    converged state, except:
151	
152	    * a route whose next hop is no longer an available direct neighbor (the
153	      failed or disconnected neighbor) becomes unreachable;
154	    * a currently available direct neighbor always advertises the direct
155	      route again, so a recovered link is usable at once;
156	    * a down router's whole row is unreachable.
157	
158	    A recovering router is handed a prior row of its own that is entirely
159	    unreachable, which leaves it knowing only itself and its currently
160	    available direct neighbors.
161	    """
162	    vectors = {}
163	    for router in ordered_nodes:
164	        if router in down_nodes:
165	            vectors[router] = _unreachable_row(ordered_nodes)
166	            continue
167	        table = {}
168	        prior = previous[router]
169	        for destination in ordered_nodes:
170	            if destination == router:
171	                table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0}
172	            elif destination in active_adjacency[router]:
173	                table[destination] = {
174	                    "nextHop": destination,
175	                    "metric": active_adjacency[router][destination],
176	                }
177	            else:
178	                entry = prior[destination]
179	                hop = entry["nextHop"]
180	                if hop is None or hop not in active_adjacency[router]:
181	                    table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
182	                else:
183	                    # A copy, so retained advertisements never alias caller
184	                    # data or later rounds.
185	                    table[destination] = dict(entry)
186	        vectors[router] = table
187	    return vectors
188

190	def distance_vector_round_infinity(
191	    previous, ordered_nodes, adjacency, down_nodes, infinity_metric
192	):
193	    """Synchronously update from prior ads with an infinity threshold.
194	
195	    Same scan/tie rules as :func:`distance_vector_round`, with no split
196	    horizon or poison reverse: every available neighbor's previous-round
197	    advertisement is read.  A candidate metric at or above
198	    ``infinity_metric`` counts as unreachable.  Down routers keep an
199	    entirely unreachable row.
200	    """
201	    current = {}
202	    for router in ordered_nodes:
203	        if router in down_nodes:
204	            current[router] = _unreachable_row(ordered_nodes)
205	            continue
206	        table = {}
207	        for destination in ordered_nodes:
208	            if destination == router:
209	                table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0}
210	                continue
211	            best_metric = None
212	            best_hop = None
213	            for neighbor in sorted(adjacency[router]):
214	                advertised = previous[neighbor][destination]
215	                if advertised["metric"] is None:
216	                    continue
217	                candidate = adjacency[router][neighbor] + advertised["metric"]
218	                if candidate >= infinity_metric:
219	                    continue
220	                # Neighbors are iterated in name order, so the first best
221	                # candidate keeps the smaller next-hop name on ties.
222	                if best_metric is None or candidate < best_metric:
223	                    best_metric = candidate
224	                    best_hop = neighbor
225	            if best_metric is None:
226	                table[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
227	            else:
228	                table[destination] = {"nextHop": best_hop, "metric": best_metric}
229	        current[router] = table
230	    return current
231	
232	
233	def distance_vector_failure_convergence(
234	    round_zero, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, down_nodes, infinity_metric
235	):
236	    """Record round 0 and every later changed round up to a fixed point.
237	
238	    After a cost increase a stale route's metric rises by at least the link
239	    cost along its dependency cycle until it reaches the threshold and is
240	    flushed as unreachable (the count-to-infinity process), so the scan
241	    always terminates; a surviving finite alternative wins earlier.
242	    """
243	    rounds = [{"round": 0, "routers": round_zero}]
244	    vectors = round_zero
245	    while True:
246	        updated = distance_vector_round_infinity(
247	            vectors,
248	            ordered_nodes,
249	            active_adjacency,
250	            down_nodes,
251	            infinity_metric,
252	        )
253	        if updated == vectors:
254	            break
255	        vectors = updated
256	        rounds.append({"round": len(rounds), "routers": vectors})
257	    return rounds
258	
259	
260	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
261	# Route hold-down (optional replay-dv suppression)
262	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
263	#
264	# A hold-down keeps a destination unreachable for a finite number of full
265	# synchronous update rounds after the router's own finite route to it was
266	# invalidated, so a possibly unstable alternative cannot be adopted at once.
267	# The suppression state is a ``{router: {destination: remaining_rounds}}``
268	# map carried *beside* the advertised vectors (never inside them): a held
269	# route still advertises exactly ``null``/``null``, so the event format, the
270	# infinity threshold, synchronous updates and tie breaks are all unchanged.
271	#
272	# An internal timer holds a *positive* remaining count while it is live:
273	#
274	# * Round 0 (immediately after an event) starts every invalidated route's
275	#   timer at ``hold_down`` and publishes that count.  Invalidation is found
276	#   as a monotone closure: a retained finite route whose selected next hop is
277	#   gone, is down, or itself advertises the destination unreachable at round 0
278	#   is itself invalidated -- and that conclusion propagates transitively.
279	# * Each later synchronous round suppresses while the carried count is
280	#   positive, then hands the next round one less.  A route invalidated later
281	#   (its selected hop's advertisement turns unusable) starts a fresh window at
282	#   that round.  More unreachability arriving inside a live window simply
283	#   keeps counting down; it never extends the window.
284	# * A destination that is a current direct neighbor is always adopted at its
285	#   direct metric, at any round, and its timer is cleared immediately.
286	# * Once the count reaches zero the *next* round rejoins ordinary selection.
287	#
288	# Down routers hold no timers; their whole row stays ``null``/``null``.
289	
290	
291	def _empty_holddowns(ordered_nodes):
292	    """A fresh ``{router: {destination: remaining}}`` map, one row per router."""
293	    return {router: {} for router in ordered_nodes}
294	
295	
296	def holddowns_public(holddowns, ordered_nodes):
297	    """A fresh sorted copy of the suppression map for published output."""
298	    return {
299	        router: {
300	            destination: holddowns[router][destination]
301	            for destination in sorted(holddowns[router])
302	        }
303	        for router in ordered_nodes
304	    }
305	
306	
307	def _holddown_round_zero_vectors(
308	    previous, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, down_nodes
309	):
310	    """Round-zero forwarding vectors under hold-down.
311	
312	    These agree with :func:`distance_vector_failure_round_zero` and then
313	    transitively null any retained finite route whose selected next hop now
314	    advertises the destination as unreachable.  Direct neighbors, self routes
315	    and down-router rows are exactly as in the legacy round zero.  The map is
316	    monotone (finite routes only become null), so iteration reaches a unique
317	    least fixed point independent of scan order.
318	    """
319	    current = distance_vector_failure_round_zero(
320	        previous, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, down_nodes
321	    )
322	    while True:
323	        updated = {}
324	        for router in ordered_nodes:
325	            if router in down_nodes:
326	                updated[router] = _unreachable_row(ordered_nodes)
327	                continue
328	            row = {}
329	            for destination in ordered_nodes:
330	                if destination == router:
331	                    row[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0}
332	                elif destination in active_adjacency[router]:
333	                    row[destination] = {
334	                        "nextHop": destination,
335	                        "metric": active_adjacency[router][destination],
336	                    }
337	                else:
338	                    entry = current[router][destination]
339	                    hop = entry["nextHop"]
340	                    if hop is None or hop not in active_adjacency[router]:
341	                        row[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
342	                    elif current[hop][destination]["metric"] is None:
343	                        # The still-present selected hop no longer offers a
344	                        # way to the destination: null it, possibly enabling
345	                        # further nulls on the next closure pass.
346	                        row[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
347	                    else:
348	                        row[destination] = dict(entry)
349	            updated[router] = row
350	        if updated == current:
351	            return current
352	        current = updated
353	
354	
355	def distance_vector_holddown_round_zero(
356	    previous, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, down_nodes, hold_down
357	):
358	    """Round 0 after an event with hold-down enabled.
359	
360	    Returns ``(vectors, holddowns)`` where every online router's previously
361	    finite, non-direct route that round zero renders unreachable starts a
362	    ``hold_down``-round timer; everything else carries no timer.
363	    """
364	    vectors = _holddown_round_zero_vectors(
365	        previous, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, down_nodes
366	    )
367	    holddowns = _empty_holddowns(ordered_nodes)
368	    if hold_down <= 0:
369	        return vectors, holddowns
370	    for router in ordered_nodes:
371	        if router in down_nodes:
372	            continue
373	        timed = holddowns[router]
374	        for destination in ordered_nodes:
375	            if destination == router or destination in active_adjacency[router]:
376	                continue
377	            prior = previous[router][destination]
378	            if (
379	                prior["nextHop"] is not None
380	                and vectors[router][destination]["metric"] is None
381	            ):
382	                timed[destination] = hold_down
383	    return vectors, holddowns
384	
385	
386	def _selected_hop_usable(
387	    router, destination, hop, previous, adjacency, infinity_metric
388	):
389	    """Whether the route currently selected via ``hop`` stays finite.
390	
391	    The same usability test an ordinary synchronous round applies to that
392	    hop's own previous-round advertisement: a present neighbor advertising
393	    unreachable, or a total metric at/above the infinity threshold, no longer
394	    carries the route.
395	    """
396	    if hop not in adjacency[router]:
397	        return False
398	    advertised = previous[hop][destination]["metric"]
399	    if advertised is None:
400	        return False
401	    return adjacency[router][hop] + advertised < infinity_metric
402	
403	
404	def distance_vector_holddown_round(
405	    previous,
406	    ordered_nodes,
407	    adjacency,
408	    down_nodes,
409	    infinity_metric,
410	    holddowns,
411	    hold_down,
412	):
413	    """One synchronous round with hold-down suppression.
414	
415	    Returns ``(vectors, holddowns)`` for the *next* round.  For an online
416	    router and a destination that is not a current direct neighbor:
417	
418	    * a live timer (positive carried count) forces ``null``/``null`` and
419	      refuses every learned finite advertisement this round; the next round
420	      receives one less, and the timer disappears at zero -- repeated
421	      unreachability never resets it;
422	    * a selected finite route whose hop has just become unusable starts a
423	      fresh window and is reported unreachable this round;
424	    * otherwise the ordinary synchronous best-neighbor scan runs, with the
425	      infinity threshold and smaller-next-hop tie rule unchanged.
426	
427	    A destination that is currently directly reachable is always adopted at
428	    its direct metric and clears any timer at once.
429	    """
430	    current = {}
431	    next_holddowns = _empty_holddowns(ordered_nodes)
432	    for router in ordered_nodes:
433	        if router in down_nodes:
434	            current[router] = _unreachable_row(ordered_nodes)
435	            continue
436	        row = {}
437	        for destination in ordered_nodes:
438	            if destination == router:
439	                row[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0}
440	                continue
441	            if destination in adjacency[router]:
442	                # Direct reachability overrides any live hold-down and clears
443	                # its timer.
444	                row[destination] = {
445	                    "nextHop": destination,
446	                    "metric": adjacency[router][destination],
447	                }
448	                continue
449	
450	            remaining = holddowns[router].get(destination)
451	            selected_hop = previous[router][destination]["nextHop"]
452	            invalidated = (
453	                remaining is None
454	                and selected_hop is not None
455	                and not _selected_hop_usable(
456	                    router,
457	                    destination,
458	                    selected_hop,
459	                    previous,
460	                    adjacency,
461	                    infinity_metric,
462	                )
463	            )
464	
465	            if invalidated:
466	                # The finite route in use failed this round; the window opens.
467	                row[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
468	                next_holddowns[router][destination] = hold_down
469	                continue
470	
471	            if remaining is not None:
472	                # Inside the suppression window: no learned finite route may
473	                # restore the destination; count the consumed round down.
474	                row[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
475	                if remaining - 1 > 0:
476	                    next_holddowns[router][destination] = remaining - 1
477	                continue
478	
479	            # No window: ordinary synchronous best-route selection.
480	            best_metric = None
481	            best_hop = None
482	            for neighbor in sorted(adjacency[router]):
483	                advertised = previous[neighbor][destination]["metric"]
484	                if advertised is None:
485	                    continue
486	                candidate = adjacency[router][neighbor] + advertised
487	                if candidate >= infinity_metric:
488	                    continue
489	                # Neighbors are iterated in name order, so the first best
490	                # candidate keeps the smaller next-hop name on ties.
491	                if best_metric is None or candidate < best_metric:
492	                    best_metric = candidate
493	                    best_hop = neighbor
494	            if best_metric is None:
495	                row[destination] = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
496	            else:
497	                row[destination] = {
498	                    "nextHop": best_hop, "metric": best_metric
499	                }
500	        current[router] = row
501	    return current, next_holddowns
502	
503	
504	def distance_vector_holddown_convergence(
505	    round_zero,
506	    holddowns_zero,
507	    ordered_nodes,
508	    active_adjacency,
509	    down_nodes,
510	    infinity_metric,
511	    hold_down,
512	):
513	    """Record rounds under hold-down until vectors and timers are both stable.
514	
515	    Round 0 is recorded as given; each later round is one synchronous
516	    hold-down update.  A round is recorded while either the forwarding
517	    vectors or the published hold-down map still change, so
518	    ``convergenceRound`` points at the last round that is not yet a fixed
519	    point under both.  Returns ``(rounds, final_vectors)``.
520	    """
521	    rounds = [
522	        {
523	            "round": 0,
524	            "routers": round_zero,
525	            "holdDowns": holddowns_public(holddowns_zero, ordered_nodes),
526	        }
527	    ]
528	    vectors = round_zero
529	    holddowns = holddowns_zero
530	    while True:
531	        updated, next_holddowns = distance_vector_holddown_round(
532	            vectors,
533	            ordered_nodes,
534	            active_adjacency,
535	            down_nodes,
536	            infinity_metric,
537	            holddowns,
538	            hold_down,
539	        )
540	        next_public = holddowns_public(next_holddowns, ordered_nodes)
541	        if (
542	            updated == vectors
543	            and next_public == rounds[-1]["holdDowns"]
544	        ):
545	            break
546	        vectors = updated
547	        holddowns = next_holddowns
548	        rounds.append(
549	            {
550	                "round": len(rounds),
551	                "routers": vectors,
552	                "holdDowns": next_public,
553	            }
554	        )
555	    return rounds, vectors

3	Public entry points:
4	
5	* :func:`compute_topology`    -> ``{"routers": ...}``
6	* :func:`converge_topology`   -> ``{"protocol", "convergenceRound", "rounds"}``

8	* :func:`replay_ls_scenario`  -> ``{"protocol", "timeline"}`` with auditable

11	  "timeline"}`` (distance-vector)

13	Each entry point takes already-decoded JSON values (plain ``dict``/``list``/
14	``str``/``int``) and returns fresh plain-Python data.  The core performs no
15	file or stream I/O, reads no command-line arguments or environment, uses no
16	module-level mutable state, and never depends on dict insertion order:
17	nodes are sorted by name and every neighbor scan is explicit.
18	
19	Inputs are deep-copied on entry and outputs are built fresh, so an input
20	object compares equal before and after a call, mutating one call's result
21	cannot affect a later call, and no fault state ever leaks between calls --
22	every replay starts from the fault-free state.

24	Invalid input raises a distinguishable error:
25

"""Pure simulation core: validated topology in, plain routing data out.

Public entry points:

* :func:`compute_topology`    -> ``{"routers": ...}``
* :func:`converge_topology`   -> ``{"protocol", "convergenceRound", "rounds"}``
* :func:`replay_scenario`     -> ``{"protocol", "timeline"}`` (link-state)
* :func:`replay_ls_scenario`  -> ``{"protocol", "timeline"}`` with auditable
  neighbor discovery, LSA flooding and per-database SPF rounds
* :func:`replay_dv_scenario`  -> ``{"protocol", "infinityMetric",
  "timeline"}`` (distance-vector)

Each entry point takes already-decoded JSON values (plain ``dict``/``list``/
``str``/``int``) and returns fresh plain-Python data.  The core performs no
file or stream I/O, reads no command-line arguments or environment, uses no
module-level mutable state, and never depends on dict insertion order:
nodes are sorted by name and every neighbor scan is explicit.

Inputs are deep-copied on entry and outputs are built fresh, so an input
object compares equal before and after a call, mutating one call's result
cannot affect a later call, and no fault state ever leaks between calls --
every replay starts from the fault-free state.

Invalid input raises a distinguishable error:

* :class:`InvalidTopology` for a malformed topology;
* :class:`InvalidScenario` for a malformed scenario;
* :class:`InvalidStateTransition` (an ``InvalidScenario`` subclass) for a
  well-formed event that requests an illegal transition.
"""
import copy

from .errors import (
    InvalidScenario,
    InvalidStateTransition,
    InvalidTopology,
    SimulationError,
)
from .linkstate import (
    active_neighbor_sets,
    baseline_databases,
    changed_endpoints,
    event_databases,
    link_state_convergence,
)
from .routing import (
    distance_vector_convergence,
    distance_vector_failure_convergence,
    distance_vector_failure_round_zero,
    distance_vector_holddown_convergence,
    distance_vector_holddown_round,
    distance_vector_holddown_round_zero,
    forwarding_table,
    initial_distance_vectors,
    link_state_snapshot,
)
from .scenario import validate_dv_scenario, validate_scenario
from .state import NetworkState, apply_event
from .topology import Topology, validate_topology

__all__ = [
    "compute_topology",
    "converge_topology",
    "replay_scenario",
    "replay_validated",
    "replay_ls_scenario",
    "replay_ls_validated",
    "replay_dv_scenario",
    "replay_dv_validated",
    "distance_vector_holddown_round",
    "distance_vector_holddown_round_zero",
    "distance_vector_holddown_convergence",
    "holddowns_public",
    "snapshot_state",
    "validate_topology",
    "validate_scenario",
    "validate_dv_scenario",
    "Topology",
    "NetworkState",
    "apply_event",
    "SimulationError",
    "InvalidTopology",
    "InvalidScenario",
    "InvalidStateTransition",
]


def _validated(topology):
    """Validate a defensive copy so caller data can never be mutated."""
    return validate_topology(copy.deepcopy(topology))


def snapshot_state(state):
    """Build one link-state routers snapshot from an explicit network state."""
    ordered_nodes = state.topology.nodes
    active_adjacency = state.active_adjacency()
    return link_state_snapshot(ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, state.down_nodes)


def compute_topology(topology):
    """Static link-state forwarding tables for a decoded topology."""
    topo = _validated(topology)
    ordered_nodes = topo.nodes
    adjacency = topo.adjacency()
    routers = {
        source: forwarding_table(source, ordered_nodes, adjacency)
        for source in ordered_nodes
    }
    return {"routers": routers}


def converge_topology(topology):
    """Distance-vector convergence rounds for a decoded topology."""
    topo = _validated(topology)
    rounds = distance_vector_convergence(topo.nodes, topo.adjacency())
    return {
        "protocol": "distance-vector",
        "convergenceRound": rounds[-1]["round"],
        "rounds": rounds,
    }


def replay_validated(topo, scenario):
    """Link-state failure timeline from an already-validated topology.

    Lets a caller (the command layer) enforce topology-before-scenario
    validation precedence.  Only the scenario is validated here.
    """
    events = validate_scenario(topo, copy.deepcopy(scenario))

    state = NetworkState.initial(topo)
    timeline = [{"event": None, "routers": snapshot_state(state)}]
    for event in events:
        state = apply_event(state, event)
        timeline.append(
            {
                "time": event.time,
                "event": event.raw,
                "routers": snapshot_state(state),
            }
        )
    return {"protocol": "link-state", "timeline": timeline}


def replay_scenario(topology, scenario):
    """Link-state failure timeline for a decoded topology and scenario.

    Always begins from the fault-free state; failure state never carries over
    from a previous call.  Each step applies one event to an immutable state
    and generates a fresh routing snapshot from the resulting explicit node
    and link availability.
    """
    return replay_validated(_validated(topology), scenario)


def replay_ls_validated(topo, scenario):
    """Auditable link-state timeline from an already-validated topology.

    Mirrors :func:`replay_validated` (topology already validated, only the
    scenario validated here) but replays the protocol itself: every timeline
    entry carries ``rounds`` (each with ``round``, ``databases`` and
    ``routers``) from round 0 through a flooding fixed point, plus the
    final ``convergenceRound``.  The baseline entry has ``event: null``;
    event entries echo ``time`` and the raw event verbatim.

    Converged databases and per-node sequence history carry from one entry
    to the next, while every *call* starts from the fault-free state.
    """
    events = validate_scenario(topo, copy.deepcopy(scenario))

    ordered_nodes = topo.nodes
    state = NetworkState.initial(topo)
    baseline_neighbors = active_neighbor_sets(
        ordered_nodes, state.active_adjacency()
    )
    databases, sequences = baseline_databases(ordered_nodes, baseline_neighbors)
    baseline_rounds, databases = link_state_convergence(
        databases,
        ordered_nodes,
        topo,
        state.active_adjacency(),
        state.down_nodes,
    )
    timeline = [
        {
            "event": None,
            "convergenceRound": baseline_rounds[-1]["round"],
            "rounds": baseline_rounds,
        }
    ]

    for event in events:
        previous_state = state
        state = apply_event(state, event)
        recovered = previous_state.down_nodes - state.down_nodes
        active_adjacency = state.active_adjacency()
        new_neighbors = active_neighbor_sets(ordered_nodes, active_adjacency)
        old_neighbors = active_neighbor_sets(
            ordered_nodes, previous_state.active_adjacency()
        )
        changed = changed_endpoints(
            ordered_nodes,
            old_neighbors,
            new_neighbors,
            state.down_nodes,
            recovered,
        )
        databases, sequences = event_databases(
            databases,
            ordered_nodes,
            new_neighbors,
            state.down_nodes,
            changed,
            sequences,
        )
        rounds, databases = link_state_convergence(
            databases,
            ordered_nodes,
            topo,
            active_adjacency,
            state.down_nodes,
        )
        timeline.append(
            {
                "time": event.time,
                "event": event.raw,
                "convergenceRound": rounds[-1]["round"],
                "rounds": rounds,
            }
        )
    return {"protocol": "link-state", "timeline": timeline}


def replay_ls_scenario(topology, scenario):
    """Auditable link-state timeline for a decoded topology and scenario.

    Always begins from the fault-free state; neither databases, sequence
    counters nor failure state carry over from a previous call, and inputs
    are deep-copied so caller data and returned data never alias.
    """
    return replay_ls_validated(_validated(topology), scenario)


def replay_dv_validated(topo, scenario):
    """Distance-vector failure timeline from an already-validated topology.

    Mirrors :func:`replay_validated` so the command layer can enforce
    topology-before-scenario precedence; here the scenario must also carry
    an ``infinityMetric`` and may carry ``holdDownRounds``.

    Without ``holdDownRounds`` the result is byte-for-byte the legacy
    document::

        {"protocol": "distance-vector", "infinityMetric": ..., "timeline": ...}

    With ``holdDownRounds`` the root echoes it and every round of every
    timeline entry additionally carries ``holdDowns`` (a router ->
    destination -> remaining-rounds map, ``{}`` when no timer is live)::

        {"protocol": "distance-vector", "infinityMetric": ...,
         "holdDownRounds": ..., "timeline": ...}

    Every timeline entry holds its converged synchronous rounds (round 0
    plus each later changed round) and a ``convergenceRound`` pointer, which
    under hold-down points at the last round in which either a forwarding
    vector or a hold-down timer still changed.  The baseline entry has
    ``event: null``; event entries echo ``time`` and the raw event verbatim.
    """
    events, infinity_metric, hold_down_rounds = validate_dv_scenario(
        topo, copy.deepcopy(scenario)
    )

    ordered_nodes = topo.nodes
    state = NetworkState.initial(topo)
    baseline_adjacency = state.active_adjacency()
    baseline_rounds = distance_vector_failure_convergence(
        initial_distance_vectors(ordered_nodes, baseline_adjacency),
        ordered_nodes,
        baseline_adjacency,
        state.down_nodes,
        infinity_metric,
    )

    if not hold_down_rounds:
        # Omission preserves the legacy result; an explicit 0 is defined to
        # disable suppression entirely, so it shares the identical path.
        return _replay_dv_legacy(
            topo, events, ordered_nodes, infinity_metric, baseline_rounds, state
        )
    return _replay_dv_holddown(
        topo,
        events,
        ordered_nodes,
        infinity_metric,
        hold_down_rounds,
        baseline_rounds,
        state,
    )


def _replay_dv_legacy(
    topo, events, ordered_nodes, infinity_metric, baseline_rounds, state
):
    """The original hold-down-free replay, unchanged in every byte."""
    timeline = [
        {
            "event": None,
            "convergenceRound": baseline_rounds[-1]["round"],
            "rounds": baseline_rounds,
        }
    ]

    vectors = baseline_rounds[-1]["routers"]
    for event in events:
        state = apply_event(state, event)
        active_adjacency = state.active_adjacency()
        round_zero = distance_vector_failure_round_zero(
            vectors, ordered_nodes, active_adjacency, state.down_nodes
        )
        rounds = distance_vector_failure_convergence(
            round_zero,
            ordered_nodes,
            active_adjacency,
            state.down_nodes,
            infinity_metric,
        )
        vectors = rounds[-1]["routers"]
        timeline.append(
            {
                "time": event.time,
                "event": event.raw,
                "convergenceRound": rounds[-1]["round"],
                "rounds": rounds,
            }
        )
    return {
        "protocol": "distance-vector",
        "infinityMetric": infinity_metric,
        "timeline": timeline,
    }


def _rounds_with_empty_holddowns(rounds, ordered_nodes):
    """Fresh copy of legacy-style rounds carrying an empty ``holdDowns`` map."""
    empty = {router: {} for router in ordered_nodes}
    return [
        {
            "round": snapshot["round"],
            "routers": snapshot["routers"],
            "holdDowns": {router: dict(empty[router]) for router in ordered_nodes},
        }
        for snapshot in rounds
    ]


def _replay_dv_holddown(
    topo,
    events,
    ordered_nodes,
    infinity_metric,
    hold_down_rounds,
    baseline_rounds,
    state,
):
    """Replay in which failure-invalidated routes are held down briefly.

    The fault-free baseline never invalidates a finite route, so its rounds
    carry empty hold-down maps and exactly the legacy forwarding vectors.
    Each event after the baseline builds its round zero from the previous
    converged vectors (whose hold-down timers have all expired by then) and
    runs the synchronous hold-down convergence.
    """
    timeline = [
        {
            "event": None,
            "convergenceRound": baseline_rounds[-1]["round"],
            "rounds": _rounds_with_empty_holddowns(baseline_rounds, ordered_nodes),
        }
    ]

    vectors = baseline_rounds[-1]["routers"]
    for event in events:
        state = apply_event(state, event)
        active_adjacency = state.active_adjacency()
        round_zero, holddowns_zero = distance_vector_holddown_round_zero(
            vectors,
            ordered_nodes,
            active_adjacency,
            state.down_nodes,
            hold_down_rounds,
        )
        rounds, vectors = distance_vector_holddown_convergence(
            round_zero,
            holddowns_zero,
            ordered_nodes,
            active_adjacency,
            state.down_nodes,
            infinity_metric,
            hold_down_rounds,
        )
        timeline.append(
            {
                "time": event.time,
                "event": event.raw,
                "convergenceRound": rounds[-1]["round"],
                "rounds": rounds,
            }
        )
    return {
        "protocol": "distance-vector",
        "infinityMetric": infinity_metric,
        "holdDownRounds": hold_down_rounds,
        "timeline": timeline,

def replay_dv_scenario(topology, scenario):

"""Acceptance tests for the I/O-free simulation core.

These tests call :mod:`packet_routing_sim.core` directly with decoded JSON
values (plain dicts/lists), never files or streams.  They pin down:

* no side effects: inputs stay equal, repeated calls share no fault state,
  and mutating one result cannot corrupt a later computation;
* distinguishable deterministic validation results (invalid topology vs
  invalid scenario vs illegal state transition);
* the published routing semantics: sorted names, smaller-hop tie breaks,
  null reachability markers, round-0/converged distance-vector shape, and a
  replay baseline identical to compute;
* failure semantics: isolated nodes, the empty topology, equal-cost paths,
  link-down surviving a node restart, reversed link endpoints, and repeated
  failure/recovery cycles;
* byte-identical results across hash seeds and declaration orders.
"""
import copy
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from packet_routing_sim.core import (
    InvalidScenario,
    InvalidStateTransition,
    InvalidTopology,
    NetworkState,
    apply_event,
    compute_topology,
    converge_topology,
    replay_dv_scenario,
    replay_ls_scenario,
    replay_scenario,
    validate_dv_scenario,
    validate_scenario,
    validate_topology,
)

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
HASH_SEEDS = tuple(
    int(seed)
    for seed in os.environ.get("PRSIM_TEST_SEEDS", "0,1,42,987654321").split(",")
)


def link(source, target, metric):
    return {"from": source, "to": target, "metric": metric}


EMPTY = {"nodes": [], "links": []}
SINGLE = {"nodes": ["solo"], "links": []}
COMPONENTS = {
    "nodes": ["a1", "a2", "b1", "b2", "iso"],
    "links": [link("a1", "a2", 2), link("b1", "b2", 5)],
}
CHAIN3 = {
    "nodes": ["A", "B", "C"],
    "links": [link("A", "B", 5), link("B", "C", 7)],
}
# Unit-metric chain so small infinity thresholds still leave the baseline
# converged and expose the full count-to-infinity progression.
DV_CHAIN = {
    "nodes": ["A", "B", "C"],
    "links": [link("A", "B", 1), link("B", "C", 1)],
}
DIAMOND = {
    "nodes": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
    "links": [
        link("A", "B", 1),
        link("A", "C", 1),
        link("B", "D", 1),
        link("C", "D", 1),
    ],
}
SQUARE = {
    "nodes": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
    "links": [
        link("A", "B", 2),
        link("B", "C", 2),
        link("C", "D", 2),
        link("D", "A", 2),
    ],
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic semantics on the validated core inputs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestCoreSemantics(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_empty_topology(self):
        self.assertEqual(compute_topology(EMPTY), {"routers": {}})
        converge = converge_topology(EMPTY)
        self.assertEqual(
            converge,
            {
                "protocol": "distance-vector",
                "convergenceRound": 0,
                "rounds": [{"round": 0, "routers": {}}],
            },
        )
        replay = replay_scenario(EMPTY, {"events": []})
        self.assertEqual(
            replay,
            {"protocol": "link-state", "timeline": [{"event": None, "routers": {}}]},
        )

    def test_single_node(self):
        routers = compute_topology(SINGLE)["routers"]
        self.assertEqual(routers["solo"]["solo"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0})
        self.assertEqual(converge_topology(SINGLE)["convergenceRound"], 0)

    def test_isolated_node_is_fully_unreachable(self):
        routers = compute_topology(COMPONENTS)["routers"]
        self.assertEqual(
            routers["iso"]["iso"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0}
        )
        for other in ("a1", "a2", "b1", "b2"):
            self.assertEqual(
                routers["iso"][other], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
            )
            self.assertEqual(
                routers[other]["iso"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
            )
        # The connected component still routes normally.
        self.assertEqual(routers["a1"]["a2"], {"nextHop": "a2", "metric": 2})

    def test_equal_cost_picks_smaller_next_hop_name(self):
        routers = compute_topology(DIAMOND)["routers"]
        self.assertEqual(routers["A"]["D"]["nextHop"], "B")
        self.assertEqual(routers["D"]["A"]["nextHop"], "B")
        self.assertEqual(routers["B"]["C"]["nextHop"], "A")
        self.assertEqual(routers["C"]["B"]["nextHop"], "A")
        square = compute_topology(SQUARE)["routers"]
        self.assertEqual(square["A"]["C"]["nextHop"], "B")
        self.assertEqual(square["C"]["A"]["nextHop"], "B")

    def test_converge_round_zero_then_only_changed_rounds(self):
        result = converge_topology(CHAIN3)
        rounds = result["rounds"]
        self.assertEqual([r["round"] for r in rounds], [0, 1])
        self.assertEqual(result["convergenceRound"], 1)
        round_zero = rounds[0]["routers"]
        # Round 0: self and directly connected neighbors only.
        self.assertEqual(round_zero["A"]["A"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": 0})
        self.assertEqual(round_zero["A"]["B"], {"nextHop": "B", "metric": 5})
        self.assertEqual(round_zero["A"]["C"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None})
        self.assertEqual(round_zero["C"]["A"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None})
        # The converged snapshot equals the link-state answer.
        self.assertEqual(
            rounds[-1]["routers"], compute_topology(CHAIN3)["routers"]
        )
        # Running one more update would change nothing (fixed point).
        from packet_routing_sim.core.routing import distance_vector_round

        ordered = ("A", "B", "C")

class TestFailureStateRules(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_link_down_survives_node_recovery(self):
        scenario = {
            "events": [
                {"time": 1, "action": "link-down", "from": "A", "to": "B"},
                {"time": 2, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"},
                {"time": 3, "action": "node-up", "node": "B"},
            ]
        }
        routers = replay_scenario(CHAIN3, scenario)["timeline"][3]["routers"]
        # B is back, but the explicitly disabled A-B link stays disabled.
        self.assertEqual(routers["A"]["B"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None})
        self.assertEqual(routers["A"]["C"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None})
        self.assertEqual(routers["B"]["C"], {"nextHop": "C", "metric": 7})

    def test_reversed_endpoints_name_the_same_link(self):
        # down A->B, up B->A must match and fully restore the baseline.
        scenario = {
            "events": [
                {"time": 1, "action": "link-down", "from": "A", "to": "B"},
                {"time": 2, "action": "link-up", "from": "B", "to": "A"},
            ]
        }
        timeline = replay_scenario(CHAIN3, scenario)["timeline"]
        self.assertEqual(
            timeline[2]["routers"], compute_topology(CHAIN3)["routers"]
        )

    def test_multiple_failures_and_recoveries(self):
        scenario = {
            "events": [
                {"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"},
                {"time": 2, "action": "node-down", "node": "C"},
                {"time": 3, "action": "link-down", "from": "A", "to": "B"},
                {"time": 4, "action": "node-up", "node": "C"},
                {"time": 5, "action": "node-up", "node": "B"},
                {"time": 6, "action": "node-down", "node": "C"},
                {"time": 7, "action": "node-up", "node": "C"},
                {"time": 8, "action": "link-up", "from": "B", "to": "A"},
            ]
        }
        timeline = replay_scenario(CHAIN3, scenario)["timeline"]
        self.assertEqual(len(timeline), 9)
        # After every recovery and the matching link-up, the network is whole
        # again: final snapshot equals the fault-free forwarding tables.
        self.assertEqual(
            timeline[-1]["routers"], compute_topology(CHAIN3)["routers"]
        )
        # Mid-scenario: both B and C down leaves A completely isolated.
        routers = timeline[2]["routers"]
        self.assertEqual(routers["A"]["B"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None})
        self.assertEqual(routers["A"]["C"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None})

    def test_each_snapshot_is_derived_from_explicit_state(self):
        topo = validate_topology(CHAIN3)
        state = NetworkState.initial(topo)
        events = validate_scenario(
            topo,
            {"events": [{"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"}]},
        )
        state = apply_event(state, events[0])
        # The state is explicit: B is down; incident links unusable.
        self.assertFalse(state.is_node_up("B"))
        self.assertTrue(state.is_node_up("A"))
        self.assertFalse(state.is_link_up("A", "B"))
        self.assertFalse(state.is_link_up("B", "C"))
        active = state.active_adjacency()
        self.assertEqual(active["A"], {})
        self.assertEqual(active["B"], {})
        self.assertEqual(active["C"], {})

    def test_apply_event_returns_new_state_without_mutating_old(self):
        topo = validate_topology(CHAIN3)
        before = NetworkState.initial(topo)
        events = validate_scenario(
            topo,
            {"events": [{"time": 1, "action": "link-down", "from": "A", "to": "B"}]},
        )
        after = apply_event(before, events[0])
        self.assertEqual(before.down_links, frozenset())
        self.assertEqual(after.down_links, frozenset({("A", "B")}))

class TestCorePurity(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_inputs_remain_equal_after_every_entry_point(self):
        for topology in (EMPTY, SINGLE, COMPONENTS, DIAMOND):
            topo_before = copy.deepcopy(topology)
            compute_topology(topology)
            converge_topology(topology)
            self.assertEqual(topology, topo_before)

        scenario = {
            "events": [
                {"time": 1, "action": "link-down", "from": "A", "to": "B"},
                {"time": 2, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"},
                {"time": 3, "action": "node-up", "node": "B"},
                {"time": 4, "action": "link-up", "from": "B", "to": "A"},
            ]
        }
        topo_before = copy.deepcopy(CHAIN3)
        scen_before = copy.deepcopy(scenario)
        replay_scenario(CHAIN3, scenario)
        self.assertEqual(CHAIN3, topo_before)
        self.assertEqual(scenario, scen_before)

    def test_repeated_calls_share_no_fault_state(self):
        fault = {
            "events": [{"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"}]
        }
        faulted = replay_scenario(CHAIN3, fault)
        self.assertIsNotNone(faulted["timeline"][-1]["routers"]["A"]["B"])
        self.assertIsNone(
            faulted["timeline"][-1]["routers"]["A"]["B"]["nextHop"]
        )
        # A fresh replay starts fault-free even though the prior call failed B.
        again = replay_scenario(CHAIN3, {"events": []})
        self.assertEqual(
            again["timeline"][0]["routers"],
            compute_topology(CHAIN3)["routers"],
        )
        # Identical inputs give structurally identical answers every time.
        self.assertEqual(
            replay_scenario(CHAIN3, fault),
            replay_scenario(CHAIN3, copy.deepcopy(fault)),
        )

    def test_mutating_a_result_cannot_pollute_later_calls(self):
        first = compute_topology(DIAMOND)
        first["routers"]["A"]["D"] = {"nextHop": "HACKED", "metric": -999}
        second = compute_topology(DIAMOND)
        self.assertEqual(
            second["routers"]["A"]["D"], {"nextHop": "B", "metric": 2}
        )

        replay1 = replay_scenario(
            CHAIN3,
            {"events": [{"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"}]},
        )
        replay1["timeline"][1]["routers"]["A"]["B"] = {"nextHop": "X", "metric": 1}
        replay1["timeline"][1]["event"]["node"] = "C"
        replay2 = replay_scenario(
            CHAIN3,
            {"events": [{"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"}]},
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            replay2["timeline"][1]["routers"]["A"]["B"],
            {"nextHop": None, "metric": None},
        )
        self.assertEqual(replay2["timeline"][1]["event"]["node"], "B")

    def test_returned_results_do_not_alias_each_other_or_input(self):
        scenario = {
            "events": [{"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"}]
        }
        result = replay_scenario(CHAIN3, scenario)
        # The echoed event is a copy, not the caller's dict.
        self.assertIsNot(
            result["timeline"][1]["event"], scenario["events"][0]
        )
        scenario["events"][0]["node"] = "C"
        self.assertEqual(result["timeline"][1]["event"]["node"], "B")

    def test_outputs_are_plain_json_serialisable_data(self):
        for value in (
            compute_topology(DIAMOND),
            converge_topology(CHAIN3),
            replay_scenario(
                DIAMOND,
                {"events": [{"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"}]},
            ),
        ):
            json.loads(json.dumps(value))

    def test_core_module_performs_no_stream_or_file_io_on_import(self):
        # The core package must not even import sys-level I/O machinery for
        # its logic; importing it must have no stdio side effects.
        source_dir = REPO_ROOT / "packet_routing_sim" / "core"
        for path in source_dir.glob("*.py"):
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertNotIn("open(", text, path)
            self.assertNotIn("sys.stdout", text, path)
            self.assertNotIn("sys.stderr", text, path)
            self.assertNotIn("sys.argv", text, path)
            self.assertNotIn("os.environ", text, path)

CHAIN4_LS = {
    "nodes": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
    "links": [link("A", "B", 1), link("B", "C", 1), link("C", "D", 1)],
}


def _db_view(entry_round):
    """{router: {originator: (sequence, neighbors)}} for one round."""
    return {
        router: None
        if database is None
        else {
            originator: (lsa["sequence"], tuple(lsa["neighbors"]))
            for originator, lsa in database.items()
        }
        for router, database in entry_round["databases"].items()
    }


class TestReplayLinkState(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_envelope_and_baseline_shape(self):
        result = replay_ls_scenario(
            CHAIN3, {"events": [{"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"}]}
        )
        self.assertEqual(set(result), {"protocol", "timeline"})
        self.assertEqual(result["protocol"], "link-state")
        timeline = result["timeline"]
        self.assertEqual(len(timeline), 2)

        baseline = timeline[0]
        self.assertEqual(set(baseline), {"event", "convergenceRound", "rounds"})
        self.assertIsNone(baseline["event"])
        for snapshot in baseline["rounds"]:
            self.assertEqual(set(snapshot), {"round", "databases", "routers"})

        event_entry = timeline[1]
        self.assertEqual(
            set(event_entry), {"time", "event", "convergenceRound", "rounds"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(event_entry["time"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(
            event_entry["event"],
            {"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"},
        )

    def test_baseline_round_zero_is_self_origination_only(self):
        baseline = replay_ls_scenario(CHAIN3, {"events": []})["timeline"][0]
        round_zero = baseline["rounds"][0]
        self.assertEqual(
            _db_view(round_zero),
            {
                "A": {"A": (1, ("B",))},
                "B": {"B": (1, ("A", "C"))},
                "C": {"C": (1, ("B",))},
            },
        )
        # Every LSA has exactly the two published fields and sorted neighbors.
        for database in round_zero["databases"].values():
            for lsa in database.values():
                self.assertEqual(set(lsa), {"sequence", "neighbors"})
        # Round 0 each router can reach only itself (it has no other LSA).
        self.assertEqual(
            round_zero["routers"]["A"]["C"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            round_zero["routers"]["B"]["A"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
        )

    def test_lsas_propagate_one_hop_per_round(self):
        baseline = replay_ls_scenario(CHAIN4_LS, {"events": []})["timeline"][0]
        self.assertEqual(baseline["convergenceRound"], 3)
        views = _db_view
        ownership = [
            {router: set(db) for router, db in views(snapshot).items()}
            for snapshot in baseline["rounds"]
        ]
        self.assertEqual(
            ownership[0],
            {"A": {"A"}, "B": {"B"}, "C": {"C"}, "D": {"D"}},
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            ownership[1],
            {
                "A": {"A", "B"},
                "B": {"A", "B", "C"},
                "C": {"B", "C", "D"},
                "D": {"C", "D"},
            },
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            ownership[2],
            {
                "A": {"A", "B", "C"},
                "B": {"A", "B", "C", "D"},
                "C": {"A", "B", "C", "D"},
                "D": {"B", "C", "D"},
            },
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            ownership[3],
            {router: {"A", "B", "C", "D"} for router in "ABCD"},
        )
        # The converged per-database SPF result is the static link-state view.
        self.assertEqual(
            baseline["rounds"][-1]["routers"],
            compute_topology(CHAIN4_LS)["routers"],
        )

    def test_rounds_are_contiguous_and_each_changes_to_a_fixed_point(self):
        for topology in (EMPTY, SINGLE, COMPONENTS, CHAIN3, DIAMOND, CHAIN4_LS):
            result = replay_ls_scenario(topology, {"events": []})
            entry = result["timeline"][0]
            numbers = [snapshot["round"] for snapshot in entry["rounds"]]
            self.assertEqual(numbers, list(range(len(numbers))), topology)
            self.assertEqual(entry["convergenceRound"], numbers[-1])
            for previous, current in zip(entry["rounds"], entry["rounds"][1:]):
                self.assertNotEqual(previous["databases"], current["databases"])

    def test_disconnected_topologies_converge_at_round_zero(self):
        # A topology whose nodes have no links at all is fixed at round 0.
        isolated = {"nodes": ["x", "y"], "links": []}
        entry = replay_ls_scenario(isolated, {"events": []})["timeline"][0]
        self.assertEqual(entry["convergenceRound"], 0)

        # COMPONENTS has two-node links: those exchange at round 1, but the
        # fully isolated node never learns anyone else's LSA.
        entry = replay_ls_scenario(COMPONENTS, {"events": []})["timeline"][0]
        self.assertEqual(entry["convergenceRound"], 1)
        round_zero = entry["rounds"][0]
        self.assertEqual(
            _db_view(round_zero)["iso"], {"iso": (1, ())}
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            _db_view(round_zero)["a1"], {"a1": (1, ("a2",))}
        )
        # Nothing is learned across components even at the fixed point, and
        # the isolated node's database never gains another originator.
        final_view = _db_view(entry["rounds"][-1])
        self.assertEqual(set(final_view["iso"]), {"iso"})
        self.assertEqual(set(final_view["a1"]), {"a1", "a2"})
        empty = replay_ls_scenario(EMPTY, {"events": []})["timeline"][0]
        self.assertEqual(
            empty,
            {
                "event": None,
                "convergenceRound": 0,
                "rounds": [{"round": 0, "databases": {}, "routers": {}}],
            },
        )

    def test_link_down_floods_and_drops_the_stale_route(self):
        scenario = {
            "events": [{"time": 1, "action": "link-down", "from": "A", "to": "B"}]
        }
        entry = replay_ls_scenario(CHAIN3, scenario)["timeline"][1]
        # A and B bump their own sequence at round 0; C is untouched.
        round_zero = entry["rounds"][0]
        self.assertEqual(
            _db_view(round_zero)["A"]["A"], (2, ())
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            _db_view(round_zero)["B"]["B"], (2, ("C",))
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            _db_view(round_zero)["C"]["C"], (1, ("B",))
        )
        # C did not change adjacency: it keeps the old view and at round 0
        # still routes to A through B using the stale mutual LSAs.
        self.assertEqual(
            round_zero["routers"]["C"]["A"], {"nextHop": "B", "metric": 12}
        )
        # One flooding round later C has B's seq-2 LSA; the A-B edge is gone
        # from every consistent view and the stale route disappears.
        self.assertEqual(entry["convergenceRound"], 1)
        final = entry["rounds"][1]
        self.assertEqual(_db_view(final)["C"]["B"], (2, ("C",)))
        self.assertEqual(
            final["routers"]["C"]["A"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            final["routers"]["C"]["B"], {"nextHop": "B", "metric": 7}
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            final["routers"]["A"]["B"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
        )

    def test_node_down_keeps_null_database_and_router_rows(self):
        scenario = {
            "events": [{"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"}]
        }
        entry = replay_ls_scenario(CHAIN3, scenario)["timeline"][1]
        for snapshot in entry["rounds"]:
            self.assertIsNone(snapshot["databases"]["B"])
            self.assertIsNone(snapshot["routers"]["B"])
            # Online routers keep a (stale) database entry for B at first.
        round_zero = entry["rounds"][0]
        self.assertEqual(_db_view(round_zero)["A"]["A"], (2, ()))
        self.assertEqual(_db_view(round_zero)["C"]["C"], (2, ()))
        # A and C are now isolated; nothing can be flooded to either side.
        self.assertEqual(entry["convergenceRound"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(
            round_zero["routers"]["A"]["C"], {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
        )

    def test_recovered_node_continues_sequence_and_relearns_neighbors(self):
        scenario = {
            "events": [
                {"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "B"},
                {"time": 2, "action": "node-up", "node": "B"},
            ]
        }
        timeline = replay_ls_scenario(CHAIN3, scenario)["timeline"]
        recovery_round_zero = timeline[2]["rounds"][0]
        # B restarts with an empty database but its own LSA continues at 2.
        self.assertEqual(
            _db_view(recovery_round_zero)["B"], {"B": (2, ("A", "C"))}
        )
        # Neighbors still carry B's old seq-1 LSA at round 0, so A can keep a
        # stale end-to-end route built from the old view; B itself knows
        # nobody yet.
        self.assertEqual(
            recovery_round_zero["routers"]["A"]["C"],
            {"nextHop": "B", "metric": 12},
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            recovery_round_zero["routers"]["B"]["A"],
            {"nextHop": None, "metric": None},
        )
        # After flooding all databases agree and tables match the baseline.
        final = timeline[2]["rounds"][-1]
        self.assertEqual(
            _db_view(final)["A"],

def _metric_view(routers):
    """{router: {destination: metric}} from a nested routing snapshot."""
    return {
        router: {dest: entry["metric"] for dest, entry in row.items()}
        for router, row in routers.items()
    }

                self.assertEqual(
                    snapshot["routers"]["C"][dest],
                    {"nextHop": None, "metric": None},
                    (snapshot["round"], dest),

        # phase converges, every one of them reports it unreachable.

class TestDistanceVectorHoldDown(unittest.TestCase):
    INF8 = 8

    def test_root_echoes_holddown_and_every_round_carries_map(self):

            set(result),

        )

            self.assertEqual(
                snapshot["holdDowns"], {"A": {}, "B": {}, "C": {}}
            )

        for snapshot in entry["rounds"]:
            self.assertEqual(set(snapshot), {"round", "routers", "holdDowns"})
            self.assertEqual(set(snapshot["holdDowns"]), {"A", "B", "C"})

    def test_node_down_holds_then_releases_to_unreachable(self):
        scenario = {
            "infinityMetric": self.INF8,
            "holdDownRounds": 2,
            "events": [{"time": 1, "action": "node-down", "node": "C"}],
        }
        entry = replay_dv_scenario(DV_CHAIN, scenario)["timeline"][1]
        rounds = entry["rounds"]
        null = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
        # Round 0: both A (via failed hop B) and B (direct neighbor C gone)
        # start a 2-round timer; every held route advertises null/null.
        self.assertEqual(rounds[0]["routers"]["A"]["C"], null)
        self.assertEqual(rounds[0]["routers"]["B"]["C"], null)
        self.assertEqual(rounds[0]["holdDowns"]["A"], {"C": 2})
        self.assertEqual(rounds[0]["holdDowns"]["B"], {"C": 2})
        # One full update round later: still held, remainder one.
        self.assertEqual(rounds[1]["routers"]["A"]["C"], null)
        self.assertEqual(rounds[1]["holdDowns"]["A"], {"C": 1})
        # The round after the remainder reached zero has an empty map and the
        # destination simply stays unreachable (no alternative exists).
        self.assertEqual(rounds[2]["holdDowns"], {"A": {}, "B": {}, "C": {}})
        self.assertEqual(rounds[2]["routers"]["A"]["C"], null)
        self.assertEqual(entry["convergenceRound"], 2)

    def test_alternative_advertisement_is_refused_then_adopted(self):
        # A reaches D through B and C at equal cost (tie -> B).  When the A-B
        # link fails, the surviving A-C-D alternative must not be adopted
        # until after the hold-down window.
        scenario = {
            "infinityMetric": self.INF8,
            "holdDownRounds": 2,
            "events": [
                {"time": 1, "action": "link-down", "from": "A", "to": "B"}
            ],
        }
        entry = replay_dv_scenario(DIAMOND, scenario)["timeline"][1]
        rounds = entry["rounds"]
        null = {"nextHop": None, "metric": None}
        # Round 0: A's route via failed hop B is null and timed.  A's own
        # route to the now-non-neighbor B is invalidated and timed as well.
        self.assertEqual(rounds[0]["routers"]["A"]["D"], null)
        self.assertEqual(rounds[0]["holdDowns"]["A"], {"B": 2, "D": 2})
        # The alternative via C (metric 2) is already advertised this round
        # but is refused throughout the window.
        self.assertEqual(rounds[1]["routers"]["A"]["D"], null)
        self.assertEqual(rounds[1]["holdDowns"]["A"], {"B": 1, "D": 1})
        self.assertEqual(rounds[2]["routers"]["A"]["D"], null)
        self.assertEqual(rounds[2]["holdDowns"]["A"], {})
        # First normal-selection round after release adopts C.
        self.assertEqual(
            rounds[3]["routers"]["A"]["D"], {"nextHop": "C", "metric": 2}
        )
        self.assertEqual(rounds[3]["holdDowns"]["A"], {})
        # convergenceRound points at the last recorded (changed) round.
        self.assertEqual(entry["convergenceRound"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(
            rounds[4]["routers"]["A"]["D"], {"nextHop": "C", "metric": 2}

        scenario = {
            "infinityMetric": 50,

        self.assertEqual(
            timeline[2]["rounds"][0]["holdDowns"]["B"], {}

        scenario = {

        # A richer multi-event scenario: every event starts from converged

97	def build_adjacency(topology):
98	    """Build an undirected adjacency map straight from the declared links."""
99	    nodes = sorted(topology["nodes"])
100	    adjacency = {node: {} for node in nodes}
101	    for edge in topology["links"]:
102	        a, b, w = edge["from"], edge["to"], edge["metric"]
103	        adjacency[a][b] = w
104	        adjacency[b][a] = w
105	    return nodes, adjacency
106	
107	
108	def floyd_warshall(nodes, adjacency):
109	    """All-pairs shortest path lengths, written independently of the SUT."""
110	    inf = float("inf")
111	    dist = {i: {j: inf for j in nodes} for i in nodes}
112	    for node in nodes:
113	        dist[node][node] = 0
114	    for a in nodes:
115	        for b, w in adjacency[a].items():
116	            # The topology validates at most one link per undirected pair.
117	            dist[a][b] = w
118	    for k in nodes:
119	        dk = dist[k]
120	        for i in nodes:
121	            di = dist[i]
122	            through_base = di[k]
123	            if through_base == inf:
124	                continue
125	            for j in nodes:
126	                candidate = through_base + dk[j]
127	                if candidate < di[j]:
128	                    di[j] = candidate
129	    return dist
130	
131	
132	def oracle_tables(topology):
133	    """Expected {(router, destination): (nextHop, metric)} via Floyd-Warshall.
134	
135	    On equal total cost the lexicographically smallest direct neighbor wins,
136	    matching the published tie-break rule.
137	    """
138	    nodes, adjacency = build_adjacency(topology)
139	    dist = floyd_warshall(nodes, adjacency)
140	    expected = {}
141	    for source in nodes:
142	        for dest in nodes:
143	            if source == dest:
144	                expected[source, dest] = (None, 0)
145	                continue
146	            if dist[source][dest] == float("inf"):
147	                expected[source, dest] = (None, None)
148	                continue
149	            winners = [
150	                neighbor
151	                for neighbor in adjacency[source]
152	                if dist[neighbor][dest] != float("inf")
153	                and adjacency[source][neighbor] + dist[neighbor][dest]
154	                == dist[source][dest]
155	            ]
156	            hop = min(winners)
157	            expected[source, dest] = (hop, dist[source][dest])
158	    return nodes, expected
159

161	def normalize(routers):
162	    """Convert JSON routing tables into {(r, d): (nextHop, metric)} tuples."""
163	    return {
164	        (r, d): (entry["nextHop"], entry["metric"])
165	        for r, row in routers.items()
166	        for d, entry in row.items()
167	    }
